name: Black Creek Corridor Dispersed Primitive Camping - De Soto National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - De Soto Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general forest dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general forest lands outside developed fee areas. Campsites set back 100ft from water bodies and designated trails.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in sandy soil layer, 200 feet from Black Creek. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. Pack out all garbage.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Clear pine needles 10 feet around fire ring. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Mississippi Forestry Commission drought burn bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway changing to unpaved gravel forest road (FS 318)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat gravel forest roads; side tracks can turn muddy after heavy Gulf rainstorms.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main gravel forest roads in dry weather)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Flat coastal plain longleaf pine savannah)

amenities: Black Creek National Recreation Trail Access

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F, warm pleasant breezes, blooming azaleas and dogwood.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (90-96°F), high mosquito / yellow fly activity, afternoon downpours.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal camping season (65-78°F daytime, 45-55°F nights), low rain.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Mild winters (50-65°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), premier winter escape.

dangers_and_hazards: Venomous snakes: Copperheads, Cottonmouths, and Eastern Diamondback Rattlesnakes
Mosquitoes and ticks near stream wetlands
High river water levels after heavy rainstorms

common_human_made_sounds: Wind blowing through longleaf pine needles

human_demographics_and_culture: Black Creek canoe paddlers, winter vanlifers, trail backpackers, and local hunters.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Choctaw indigenous traditions revere the Black Creek blackwater river and longleaf pine forests as sacred ancestral spirit lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Peaceful pine savannah grounding energy, gentle winter climate, serene blackwater river reflections.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding blackwater river trail through pine savannah and oxbow lakes

public_reviews_summary: Top choice for winter boondocking in Mississippi. Tranquil longleaf pine forest, great blackwater river access, and reliable cell service.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Great solar panel output.
